get.summary:
Audit trail: who called what, when, and whether it was allowed. Persisted
in the database, which lives on the controller's replicated volume, so the
history follows the controller across a failover instead of being split
across the journals of whichever nodes happened to be active.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: newest first; 0 means a server-chosen default

parameters.name: method
parameters.description: exact match filter, empty for all

parameters.name: failuresOnly
parameters.description: only entries whose result is not OK

post.summary:
Backup operations: shipping point-in-time copies OFF the cluster to an
S3-compatible object store, an SMB share or a WebDAV endpoint.
post.description:
Distinct from snapshots (same pool, lost with the machine) and from WAN DR
(a replica, where a delete replicates). Every backup is a FULL image; there
is no incremental mode.

parameters.name: node
parameters.description:
node optionally selects which node reaches the target to delete the
objects; empty uses the node that wrote the backup.

parameters.name: force
parameters.description: force drops the record even when the objects could not be removed.

get.summary:
Operational notifications: a replica degraded, a resource's Primary moved,
a node stopped answering. ListEvents serves the controller's bounded
in-memory history — enough to see what just happened, not an archive. The
durable record of who did what is ListAuditEvents.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: newest first; 0 means a server-chosen default

parameters.name: types
parameters.description: exact type matches; empty for all

parameters.name: sinceId
parameters.description:
Only events newer than this id. Lets a client resume where it left off
instead of re-reading the whole buffer.

get.summary:
WatchEvents streams notifications as they happen, so an operator (or the
web UI, or a script) can react without polling. Over REST this is a
newline-delimited JSON stream; `curl -N .../v1/events/watch` works.
get.description:
A watcher that cannot keep up loses events rather than blocking the
controller. Event.id is monotonic across the whole stream, so a gap in it
is how a client detects that it fell behind.

parameters.name: sinceId
parameters.description:
Replay retained events newer than this id before streaming live ones, so a
reconnecting client does not miss what happened while it was away. 0 skips
the replay and starts from now.

get.summary: HA OCF resource-agent discovery and drbd-reactor promoter TOML editing.

The controller's own log output, from an in-memory ring buffer. Deliberately
not persisted: this is for watching what a running controller is doing, and
a controller that has moved has nothing useful to say about its old node.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: newest first; 0 means a server-chosen default

post.summary:
Storage tiering: put an SSD/NVMe device in front of one node's LVM pool
with lvmcache. The cache serves the whole pool, and defaults to
writethrough because a writeback cache holds acknowledged writes that no
other node has yet.

ConvertPoolToThin rebuilds one node's LVM pool as a thin pool, in place.
Thick pools cannot hold a snapshot history: each snapshot reserves a fixed
COW area whether anything changes or not.

RepairWanProxy reconciles a WAN resource's replication tunnels with what
the controller currently believes its nodes are: it re-provisions the legs
that should exist and removes instances left behind by a node that was
renumbered or removed. Safe to run on a healthy resource — it converges.

PopulateVolume copies a source block device (an LVM/ZFS snapshot, or another
resource's backing volume) into an ALREADY-CREATED, still-empty DRBD
resource. Unlike RestoreSnapshot — which merges a snapshot back into its own
origin in place — this fills a *different*, new volume, which is what CSI
restore-from-snapshot and volume cloning need.
post.description:
The copy is written to the target's DRBD device (not its backing LV) on a
node that holds a replica, so DRBD replicates it to every peer for free.

parameters.name: resource
parameters.description: resource / volume_id identify the freshly created, still-empty target.

drNode.title: registered node that will hold the remote copy

drEndpoint.title: public address the primary site dials

egressAddress.title: optional source address for the primary site

SDSControllerAddDRBody.description:
AddDRRequest attaches an asynchronous off-site replica to a resource that is
already running, turning a LAN cluster into the two-site shape in place.

device.description: Block device on that node to spend entirely on cache, e.g. /dev/nvme0n1.

mode.description:
"writethrough" (the default when empty) or "writeback". writeback
acknowledges a write once it is on the SSD, so losing that one SSD loses
every write it had not yet destaged, recoverable only from a replica that
happens to hold them.

SDSControllerAddReplicaBody.description:
AddReplicaRequest adds a diskful local replica to a running resource. On a
two-site resource the new node also gets its own WAN leg to the DR: DRBD 9 is
a full mesh, and a replica the DR cannot reach ends replication the moment it
is promoted.

SDSControllerAdoptResourceBody.description:
AdoptResourceRequest imports an already-existing (foreign) DRBD resource into
SDS management by recording its metadata in the SDS database. It never
creates or modifies the actual DRBD resource or its data. Every field except
name is optional and auto-discovered from the live .res on a node when
omitted; a provided value overrides discovery.

SDSControllerAttachDisklessClientBody.description:
AttachDisklessClient adds a node to a resource as a diskless data client: it
stores no local replica but connects over DRBD and can be promoted Primary to
read/write the volume over the network. Distinct from a quorum tiebreaker,
which is never promoted. Idempotent.

ocfAgents.title: optional OCF agents appended to promoter start[]

startItems.description:
start_items, when non-empty, defines the promoter start[] list verbatim and
in order (systemd units and OCF agents interleaved). The legacy fields
2/3/5/6 above are then used only for provisioning side effects (mount unit
generation, VIP service-ip precondition) and NOT for start[] ordering.

sourceDevice.description:
source_device is the block device to copy FROM, on `node`: an LVM snapshot
(/dev/<vg>/<snap>), a ZFS zvol, or another resource's backing volume.

node.description:
node must hold a diskful replica of `resource` AND have source_device
locally; the copy runs entirely on that node.

dryRun.description:
DryRun reports what would change without touching anything. Worth using
first: repair restarts replication tunnels.

resource.description:
resource is the resource to restore INTO; empty restores into the resource
the backup was taken from. It must exist, be large enough, and not be in
use.

enable.description:
enable=true is strict: WAN (protocol A / async) resources are REFUSED,
because two Primaries over an async link corrupts data, and a failure on
any node fails the call.

enable=false is idempotent: it is the caller's cleanup path, so an unknown
resource or a node that rejects the command is tolerated — but the
effective state is verified afterwards and an error is returned if any
reachable node is still dual-primary.

SDSControllerSetDualPrimaryBody.description:
SetDualPrimary toggles DRBD's allow-two-primaries for a resource. It exists
for the live-migration hand-off in the Proxmox VE storage plugin, where the
source and target hypervisor both hold the disk open for a moment.

The toggle is applied at RUNTIME only (drbdadm net-options) and never written
into the .res file, so a reboot or `drbdadm adjust` restores single-primary
on its own.

SDSControllerSetNodeLabelsBody.description:
SetNodeLabels sets or merges key=value labels on a node. When replace is
true the node's labels are replaced wholesale; otherwise the given labels are
merged in (a label with an empty value deletes that key).

quorumGuarded.description:
quorum_guarded requests a SAFE hard-failover promote: the controller tries
a normal (non-forced) promote first and only escalates to `drbdadm primary
--force` if the target node currently holds DRBD quorum (majority). If the
node lacks quorum the promote is REFUSED (forcing without quorum could
split-brain). When set, `force` is ignored. Used by the CSI node plugin so
a Pod rescheduled after a hard node failure promotes the survivor iff it is
safe to do so.

SDSControllerSetTiebreakerBody.description:
SetTiebreakerRequest moves a resource's diskless quorum tiebreaker to
another node. An empty node removes the tiebreaker without adding one.

options.description:
DRBD options as "section/key" -> value (e.g. "net/max-buffers" -> "8000",
"on-no-quorum" -> "suspend-io"). Keys without a section default to the
resource-level "options" section.

user.description: user is the S3 access key id, or the SMB/WebDAV username.

secret.description:
secret is the S3 secret access key, or the SMB/WebDAV password. It is
write-only: it is never returned by any RPC. Clients are expected to read
it from an environment variable or a file rather than a command-line flag.

secretObscured.description: secret_obscured says secret is already in rclone's obscured form.

mode.description:
The mode actually applied, so a caller that sent nothing learns it got
writethrough rather than assuming.

nodes.description: Discovered/recorded metadata, echoed back for the caller to display.

client.title: caller address, forwarded client IP when proxied

user.title: empty when RBAC is off: no identity exists

node.description:
Node that served the call. The controller relocates, so a trail spanning a
failover is otherwise ambiguous about where each entry came from.

state.description: state is running | completed | failed. Only completed is restorable.

description.description: description is a rendered one-line summary for display.

v1BackupTargetInfo.description:
BackupTargetInfo describes a backup repository. The secret is intentionally
absent: a credential readable back out of the API leaks through every client
that ever renders it.

fields.description: Structured zap fields, rendered as strings so the UI needs no type table.

volumes.description:
Volumes rebuilt on this node; each is resyncing in full from its peers
when the call returns.

node.description:
node optionally pins which replica is snapshotted and read. Empty prefers
an UpToDate Secondary.

sizeGb.title: single-volume shorthand; ignored when `volumes` is set

pool.title: single-volume shorthand; ignored when `volumes` is set

volumes.description:
volumes lists one or more DRBD volumes to create atomically (volume 0..N).
When empty, a single volume is created from size_gb/pool for back-compat.

wan.description:
WAN replication (opt-in add-on). Absent/false ⇒ LAN, behaves exactly as
before. `wan` is the master switch; without it the dr_* fields are rejected.
See docs/2026-07-05-wan-replication-design.md.

route this resource over the internet via a per-resource sds-proxy pair

drNode.title: the DR-site node (must be a registered node); WAN only

drEndpoint.title: the DR site's public WAN address the primary dials; WAN only

wanPort.title: WAN mTLS port (default a random >3000 per resource); WAN only

wanEgressAddress.description:
wan_egress_address optionally pins the source address the primary's proxy
binds before dialing the DR site, so replication leaves over a chosen
interface (e.g. a leased line) and reaches the DR firewall from a
predictable source IP. Empty lets the primary's routing table decide.

replicas.description:
replicas requests auto-placement: when `nodes` is empty the controller
picks this many nodes (most free space in the target pool first). Ignored
when `nodes` is set. 0 means "not auto-placing" unless nodes is also empty,
in which case the controller defaults to 2.

replicasOnDifferent.title:
replicas_on_different names node-label keys (e.g. "rack"); during
auto-placement each replica is put in a distinct value of every listed
label, so a single fault domain never holds two replicas. Only nodes
carrying the labels participate. Empty = capacity-only. Ignored when `nodes`
is set. (Wire-compatible successor of the earlier singular string field.)

replicasOnSame.description:
replicas_on_same names node-label keys whose value must be IDENTICAL across
all replicas (e.g. keep every copy in one zone). Composable with
replicas_on_different. Ignored when `nodes` is set.

doNotPlaceWith.description:
do_not_place_with names other resources; auto-placement will not put a
replica on any node already holding a replica of them (cross-resource
anti-affinity). Ignored when `nodes` is set.

encrypt.description:
encrypt puts a LUKS2 container between DRBD and the backing LVM/ZFS volume
on every replica, so the pool disks hold ciphertext. This is encryption AT
REST ONLY: DRBD sits ABOVE the crypt layer, so replication traffic between
nodes is the same plaintext it always was. Chosen once, at creation: there
is no in-place conversion, and asking for one on a resource that already
exists is refused rather than half-applied.

node.title: node that keeps running the standalone controller

resourcesMoved.description: resources_moved lists the DRBD resources whose Primary was moved off the node.

vip.title: virtual IP for the controller (CIDR, required)

pool.title: storage pool backing the metadata resource

port.title: DRBD port for the metadata resource (default 7999)

handoffLog.title: node-local log path of the handoff script

id.description:
Monotonic across the controller's whole event stream, starting at 1. A
watcher whose ids skip a value knows it fell behind and lost events.

status.description:
"firing" when a condition starts, "resolved" when it clears, "info" for
one-shot events that do neither. Pairing these is how a receiver avoids
treating a recovery as a new problem.

resource.title: empty for events not scoped to a resource

node.title: empty for events not scoped to a node

details.description:
Type-specific fields: disk_state / repl_state for degrade events,
from / to for failover events.

v1Event.description:
Event is one operational notification. The same shape is delivered to
Webhook receivers as JSON, so a receiver written against one works against
the other.

v1GFSRetention.description:
GFSRetention is a grandfather-father-son retention policy: how many
snapshots to keep per time bucket. Zero disables a bucket.

activeNode.title: node currently running the controller (DRBD Primary)

v1HaStartItem.description:
HaStartItem is one entry in the promoter start[] list. systemd/mount units and
OCF resource agents are PEERS: the list is a single ordered sequence and each
item is exactly one of the fields below. This is what lets a correct stack be
expressed (e.g. portblock -> Filesystem -> IPaddr2 -> nfsserver -> exportfs ->
portunblock) instead of forcing all OCF agents after all systemd units.

total.description: Entries held in total, so the UI can say whether it is showing everything.

node.description: The node whose ring buffer this is — the active controller, whichever it is.

truncated.description: True when the buffer has wrapped, i.e. older lines have been discarded.

published.description:
Total published since the controller started. Compared against the oldest
id returned, this tells a client whether history has been discarded.

dropped.description: Events dropped because a subscriber could not keep up.

labels.description:
labels are arbitrary key=value tags on the node (e.g. rack=A, zone=east)
used by placement constraints like replicas_on_different.

replicationAddress.description:
replication_address is the address DRBD uses for this node. Empty means it
shares `address` (the historical single-network setup).

syncPercent.description:
Percent of this peer's data in sync (0..100). 100 when steady-state / not
resyncing. Only meaningful for a peer whose replication_state is a resync
state (SyncSource/SyncTarget/PausedSync*).

node.description:
node is the SDS node name this state belongs to. The map itself is keyed by
DRBD host name, which is the machine's real hostname and generally is NOT
the node name the rest of the API uses — so without this a caller cannot
pair a state with the entry of `nodes` it describes.

v1OcfAgent.description:
OcfAgent is one OCF resource-agent entry to compose into an HA promoter's
start[] list. It renders as "ocf:<provider>:<name> <instance> <k>=<v> ...".

cached.description:
Storage tiering (lvmcache). A pool with no fast tier reports cached=false
and leaves the rest zero, so a tiered pool is distinguishable from a plain
one in a plain `pool list`.

cacheSizeBytes.description: Size of the fast device given to the cache.

cacheUsedPercent.description:
Kernel dm-cache counters, rounded to whole percent. hit_percent is
cumulative since the cache was last activated, not a moving average.

cacheDirtyPercent.description:
Share of the cache holding writes that have not reached the slow device.
Zero on a writethrough cache by construction; on a writeback cache this is
the size of the window that a lost SSD would take with it.

cacheDevice.description: The fast block device backing the cache, as the node names it.

cacheDegraded.description:
True when LVM reports the cache as unhealthy — a cache in this state
cannot be flushed, so it cannot be detached without discarding data.

bytesCopied.description: bytes_copied is what dd reported, for logging and progress reporting.

members.description:
members is every node in the resource config: diskful replicas, diskless
tiebreakers and diskless clients alike. DRBD counts them all.

required.description: required is the majority DRBD needs to keep serving: members/2 + 1.

online.description:
online is how many members the reporting node can currently see, itself
included.

hasQuorum.description:
has_quorum is what DRBD itself reports, not a recomputation of the fields
above — they can disagree while a connection is being established, and DRBD
is the one that decides whether I/O proceeds.

tolerated.description:
tolerated is how many further members can be lost before I/O suspends.
Negative is not possible; zero means the next failure stops the resource.

v1QuorumInfo.description: QuorumInfo is the vote arithmetic behind "will this resource survive?".

replicationAddress.description:
replication_address is the address DRBD uses for this node in generated
.res files, letting replication traffic ride a dedicated NIC/subnet while
the controller keeps reaching the node over `address` (SSH/management).
Empty means "same as address", which is the historical behavior.

expectedLegs.description: Legs the resource should have, as "<node> -> <leg id>".

removedLegs.description: Instances removed (or, under dry_run, that would be), as "<host>: <leg id>".

disklessNodes.description: Nodes participating only as diskless quorum tiebreakers (vote, no data).

quorumRisk.description:
True when the resource has two diskful nodes and no tiebreaker, so a
single node failure suspends I/O (no quorum majority).

disklessClients.description:
Nodes attached as diskless data clients: no local replica, but connected
over DRBD and promotable to serve the volume over the network. Distinct
from diskless_nodes (quorum-only tiebreakers).

wanMode.description:
WAN replication: wan_mode marks a resource with an off-site asynchronous
copy, and dr_node names which of `nodes` holds it. Without this the list
shows the DR as just another replica, which is exactly wrong — it is a
different site, a different protocol, and it never takes over automatically.

encrypted.description:
encrypted is true when every replica's backing volume is a LUKS2 container
(DRBD → LUKS → LVM/ZFS). Encryption at rest only — DRBD replicates the
plaintext, so the wire is not protected by this.

wan.description:
WAN replication (all empty/false for an ordinary LAN resource). When wan is
true this resource replicates over the internet via a per-resource sds-proxy
pair (protocol A / async), so the DR peer can lag; wan_proxy reports each
WAN node's `sds-proxy@<resource>` unit state (active/inactive/...).

wanReachable.description:
wan_reachable is true when the primary node can currently open a TCP
connection to the DR WAN endpoint (i.e. the DR firewall/security group
permits the mTLS port). False here explains a WAN resource that is up
locally but not replicating.

wanMetrics.description:
wan_metrics carries the counters sds-proxy publishes on the primary. Absent
when they could not be read (older proxy, first tick not yet written, node
unreachable) — absent means UNKNOWN, not zero.

quorum.description:
quorum is what decides whether this resource keeps serving when nodes are
lost. It is the one number that governs availability and it was previously
reported nowhere: an operator had to know DRBD counts every configured node
(tiebreakers and the off-site DR included) and work out the majority by hand.

encrypted.description:
encrypted mirrors ResourceInfo.encrypted: the backing volumes are LUKS2
containers. Reported here because "is this volume encrypted?" is a question
an auditor asks of the running system, not of the creation request.

pool.description: Storage pool (volume group) backing this volume.

backingVolume.description:
Backing logical volume name inside the pool (e.g. "<resource>_data").
Combined with pool it forms the "<pool>/<lv>" path used by snapshot APIs.

encrypted.description:
encrypted is true when DRBD consumes this volume through a LUKS2 container
rather than the backing LV/zvol directly. Snapshots of an encrypted volume
are snapshots of the ciphertext.

v1VolumeSpec.description:
VolumeSpec is one DRBD volume within a resource. storage_type comes from the
resource; each volume may target its own pool.

bufferUsedBytes.description:
buffer_used_bytes is the un-replicated backlog: writes the primary's DRBD
has already acknowledged to its application that have NOT yet reached the
DR site. Under protocol A this IS the data-loss window of a DR failover
performed right now — the question `resource status` previously could not
answer.

drbdToWanBytes.description:
Payload accepted from DRBD versus bytes actually put on the WAN, and the
ratio between them: the compression the link is really achieving.

reconnects.description:
reconnects climbing on an otherwise healthy link is the signature of a
flapping path; ring_full_events non-zero means the WAN could not keep up
with the write workload and DRBD was pushed into Ahead.

v1WANMetrics.description: WANMetrics is what the primary site's sds-proxy reports about the WAN leg.
